title: STORY TIME: How lifting changed my life
summary: Filmed in a forest, NH recounts being the smallest, weakest kid, bullied daily and treated with contempt even by adults, then turning violent, then finding his way out through thousands of hours of solitary training. He argues lifting transforms the spirit more than the body, that looking strong buys a peaceful life, and that only the strong can be truly kind.
claims: As a kid he was the smallest in class, could not do a single push-up or leg raise, and was beaten up almost daily
He fought back by becoming more violent than the bullies; it stopped the beatings but left him insecure and he lashed out at people he loved
How people treat you shapes how you see yourself and vice versa, creating a vicious cycle
Kind people who let others trample them eventually start to hate people; the softest hearts need the toughest walls
People treat you in three ways: indifference, bullying or pity; he hated pity more than bullying
To change you must destroy your weak identity, which requires isolation rather than seeking comfort from others
He spent thousands of hours training alone
Choosing when to suffer is a superpower: voluntary suffering in training makes all other pain easier to shrug off
What he was really after was transformation of the spirit; the body was a byproduct
Humans sense weakness and strength; people get mistreated for a small character, though small body and small spirit usually go together
Looking strong matters more than being strong: he cannot fight trained people, but his body earns him the peaceful life he always wanted
Muscle brings a halo effect: people treat you with more respect, attraction and admiration
Most lifters lift to be left alone and to master themselves and their destiny, not to dominate others
Only the strong can be truly kind; a weak person's niceness is camouflaged cowardice
Lifting shapes the body to match the spirit; a body that feels like both a home and a castle is what confidence is
One day, after six months or six years, you wake up and love yourself; you cannot predict when
Lifting would fix most psychological problems such as social anxiety, which he used to suffer from
He was never suicidal but had started questioning whether to put in effort at all
Five years earlier he would never have believed he would look and feel like this
Your physique reminds others of their potential: a neighbor seeing him shirtless said he needed to start working out again
